checks_performed: Read the exact target and the draft as the only evidentiary inputs; no web or other source files were used.
Independently reconstructed the quadratic-character counts, conference-matrix identity, Fourier linear program, Jacobi-sum representation, and spectral theta certificates.
Independently proved the theta product, induced-subgraph monotonicity, disjoint-union additivity, Paley self-complementarity, and the resulting two-sided asymptotic bounds.

Created and ran an exact-arithmetic checker using integers, Fraction, and Q(√2). It verified the small-prime Fourier certificates and exhaustively checked all p=17 perfect matchings and vertex permutations.
Compared the final writeup directly with the requested limit statement, independently of claimed_resolution and self_assessment.

claims.claim: Writing Q for the nonzero squares and K_p=complement(H_p), both H_p and K_p are Cayley graphs on the multiplicative group Q. Their connection sets S and T have sizes (p−5)/4 and (p−1)/4, respectively.
claims.evidence: For x,y∈Q, χ(x−y)=χ(x/y−1), so adjacency depends only on x/y. Thus S={q≠1:χ(q−1)=1} and T={q:χ(q−1)=−1}; χ(−1)=1 makes both inverse-closed. Using 1_Q(x)=(1+χ(x))/2 gives Σ_{q∈Q}χ(q−1)=−1 from the two standard sums Σ_{x≠0}χ(x−1)=−1 and Σ_xχ(x(x−1))=−1. Together with |S|+|T|=(p−3)/2, this yields the claimed sizes. The checker additionally confirms p=5,13,17 exactly.
claims.search_method: Direct finite-field character calculation, supplemented by exact small-prime checks.

claims.claim: The localized Paley sign matrix B has operator norm at most √p, by an exact conference-matrix identity.
claims.evidence: For C_{xy}=χ(x−y), the quadratic-character correlation gives C²=pI−J. Ordering the field as {0}, Q, and {ν/q:q∈Q} for a nonsquare ν gives blocks C=[[0,1ᵀ,−1ᵀ],[1,B,D],[−1,D,−B]], with D symmetric. The Q,Q block of C²=pI−J is J+B²+D²=pI−J, hence B²+D²=pI−2J. Therefore ||Bv||²=p||v||²−2(1ᵀv)²−||Dv||²≤p||v||² for every real v.
claims.search_method: Exact block multiplication and the quadratic-character correlation identity.

claims.claim: θ(K_p) is exactly an explicit finite Fourier linear program, or equivalently a nonnegative-vector problem for a half-dimensional Fourier projection.
claims.evidence: Averaging a feasible theta matrix over multiplication by Q preserves feasibility and objective and gives X_{xy}=f(x⁻¹y)/n. Trace, edge-zero, symmetry, and PSD become f(1)=1, f|_T=0, f(q)=f(q⁻¹), and nonnegative Fourier coefficients. The objective is Σ_qf(q). With y_ψ=f̂(ψ)/n, Fourier inversion gives y≥0, Σy=1, and θ(K_p)=n y_triv. Since D={1}∪S has |D|=n/2, support of f in D is exactly membership of y in the range of the Fourier conjugate of the coordinate projection onto D, namely P_Dy=y. Pairing conjugate character coordinates supplies the required real symmetric matrices without changing the optimum.
claims.search_method: Automorphism averaging followed by finite abelian Fourier inversion and support/projection duality.

claims.claim: Every nontrivial Fourier eigenvalue of B is the real part of a Jacobi sum of modulus √p.
claims.evidence: For nontrivial ψ on Q, choose an extension A to F_p^*. Neither A nor Aχ is trivial. The eigenvalue is R_ψ=Σ_{q∈Q}ψ(q)χ(q−1)=[J(A,χ)+J(Aχ,χ)]/2. All characters and products entering these Jacobi sums are nontrivial, so both sums have modulus √p. Gauss-sum identities give J(A,χ)J(Aχ,χ)=G(χ)²=χ(−1)p=p. Two modulus-√p numbers with product p are complex conjugates, making their average Re J(A,χ).
claims.search_method: Character extension plus exact Gauss-sum and Jacobi-sum identities, with all exceptional-character cases checked.

claims.claim: For every vertex-transitive graph G on n vertices, θ(G)θ(complement(G))=n.
claims.evidence: The theta dual is min t with tI+Z−J⪰0 and Z supported on edges. Any such certificate M gives (M+J)/(nt) as a complement-primal feasible matrix with objective at least n/t, proving the product is at least n. Conversely, average an optimal primal X over a transitive automorphism group. Then diag(X)=1/n and X1=(θ(G)/n)1. Hence (n²/θ(G))X−J⪰0; its off-diagonal support is contained in the complement edges and its diagonal coefficient is n/θ(G), so it is a complement-dual certificate. This gives the reverse inequality.
claims.search_method: Direct primal-dual SDP proof with transitive automorphism averaging.

claims.claim: Theta is monotone under taking induced subgraphs.
claims.evidence: If L is an induced subgraph of G, extend any feasible theta matrix for L by zero rows and columns on V(G)\V(L). PSD, trace, objective, and every edge-zero constraint are preserved, so θ(L)≤θ(G).
claims.search_method: Direct zero-extension of primal feasible matrices.

claims.claim: Theta is additive on disjoint unions: θ(G⊔L)=θ(G)+θ(L).
claims.evidence: In a Gram representation, the objective is the squared norm of the total vector sum. If the G and L blocks have traces a and b, their sum-vector norms are at most √(aθ(G)) and √(bθ(L)); triangle inequality and Cauchy–Schwarz give an objective at most (a+b)(θ(G)+θ(L)). For the reverse inequality, take optimal Gram families, rotate their sum vectors into the same direction, and choose a=θ(G)/(θ(G)+θ(L)), b=θ(L)/(θ(G)+θ(L)). The resulting feasible union solution has objective θ(G)+θ(L).
claims.search_method: Gram-factorization proof using aligned vector sums and Cauchy–Schwarz.

claims.claim: The full Paley graph P_p satisfies θ(P_p)=√p.
claims.evidence: Translations make P_p vertex-transitive, while multiplication by any nonsquare is an isomorphism from P_p to its complement. The verified vertex-transitive product identity therefore gives θ(P_p)²=p. Positivity selects θ(P_p)=√p.
claims.search_method: Paley translation symmetry, nonsquare self-complementarity, and the theta product identity.

claims.evidence: Multiplication by a fixed nonsquare maps K_p isomorphically onto the Paley subgraph induced by the nonsquares N. Vertex 0 has no Paley neighbor in N because χ(−1)=1, so P_p[{0}∪N] is K_p disjoint-union one isolated vertex. Induced-subgraph monotonicity, additivity, and θ(P_p)=√p give θ(K_p)+1≤√p.
claims.search_method: Explicit nonsquare relabeling followed by induced-subgraph monotonicity and additivity.

claims.evidence: H_p is d=(p−5)/4 regular on n=(p−1)/2 vertices, and A=(B+J−I)/2. Every nontrivial adjacency eigenvalue is (R_ψ−1)/2, so its least eigenvalue τ satisfies τ≥−(√p+1)/2. For a d-regular graph, tI+cA−J with c=n/(d−τ) and t=−nτ/(d−τ) is theta-dual feasible, yielding θ≤−nτ/(d−τ). This expression decreases with τ; substituting the stated lower bound gives (√p+1)²/(√p+3). For p=5, H_p is the empty two-vertex graph and both sides equal 2.
claims.search_method: Fourier spectral bound followed by an explicit theta-dual ratio certificate, including the p=5 exception.

claims.evidence: The upper bound is claim 8. Since H_p is a Cayley graph and hence vertex-transitive, θ(H_p)θ(K_p)=n. Dividing n=(p−1)/2 by the verified upper bound (√p+1)²/(√p+3) for θ(H_p) gives exactly ((√p−1)(√p+3))/(2(√p+1)).
claims.search_method: Exact algebraic combination of the complementary-theta product with the two verified upper bounds.

claims.claim: The proven bounds imply 1/√2≤liminf θ(K_p)/√(p/2)≤limsup θ(K_p)/√(p/2)≤√2, and isolate the unresolved step as asymptotic balance of the complementary theta numbers.
claims.evidence: Dividing the lower and upper bounds by √(p/2) gives limiting constants 1/√2 and √2. With n=(p−1)/2 and θ(H_p)θ(K_p)=n, the requested limit is equivalent to θ(K_p)/√n→1, equivalently θ(H_p)/√n→1. Thus asymptotic equality of the complementary theta numbers is exactly the missing step, and the displayed interval does not itself prove convergence.
claims.search_method: Exact normalization of the two-sided bounds and use of the complementary-theta product.

claims.claim: The exact small-prime values are θ(K_5)=1, θ(K_13)=2, θ(K_17)=8−4√2; correspondingly θ(H_5)=2, θ(H_13)=3, and θ(H_17)=2+√2.
claims.evidence: The checker verifies the finite-field connection sets and exact Fourier primal/dual certificates. For p=13, a=1/2 is feasible and the l=3 inequality 1−2a≥0 proves optimality. For p=17, a=2−√2 and b=3−2√2 are Fourier-feasible, while the positive exact combination (4−2√2)L_3+(3−2√2)L_4 bounds 2a+b by 7−4√2. This gives 8−4√2. The p=5 value is immediate from K_5=K_2. Multiplication with the stated complementary values gives n exactly in all three cases.
claims.search_method: Exact finite-field construction and exact Fourier primal/dual certification in Q and Q(√2).
claims.witness: p=5,13,17; the checker records exact optimal Fourier certificates and exact complementary products.

claims.claim: A tempting exact explanation—K_p being a relabelled copy of H_p with one perfect matching added—is already false for p=17.
claims.evidence: For p=17 the checker constructs H_17=Cay(Z/8Z,{1,4,7}) and K_17=Cay(Z/8Z,{2,3,5,6}), enumerates all 14 perfect matchings of K_17, and checks every deletion exactly. Twelve deletions contain a triangle, whereas H_17 is triangle-free. The other two have six induced 4-cycles, whereas H_17 has four. Exhaustive permutation checks also find zero isomorphisms. Thus no matching deletion of K_17 is a relabelled H_17.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive integer graph enumeration over all perfect matchings and all vertex permutations.

target_evidence: The exact target requires proving that θ(complement(H_p))/√(p/2) tends to 1, or rigorously proving that it does not. The draft proves neither: its bounds only place the liminf and limsup between 1/√2 and √2, and its product/projection formulations explicitly leave asymptotic balance unresolved. These are nevertheless correct, nonvacuous Θ(√p) bounds and exact structural reductions, so they constitute VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS. The final writeup expressly says that it does not prove the requested limit, so it does not overclaim target coverage. Accordingly, the draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is ACCURATE.
